template.name: Internet Foyer
template.reusable_market: Personal PR base for individuals, operators, makers, small studios, and small businesses.

positioning.first_impression: This person has taste, range, and something worth clicking into.
positioning.curiosity_strategy: Show a few high-signal doors instead of explaining the whole person on the root.
must_feel_like: a front room on the internet
a curated glimpse into a real life
someone who likes themself without performing
professional and personal at the same time

audience_modes.intent: Find proof quickly without reading a full bio.
Understand what Justin makes and where deeper work lives.
Decide whether this person is organized enough to contact.
Get a human read without exposing private life.

reference_set.role: Plain personal index with strong signal density.
borrow: projects and writing doing the credibility work
avoid: becoming too plain for a reusable brand system

borrow: modular motion as proof of craft
small interactive moments that invite poking
avoid: library-site technical density on a personal root

borrow: projects, writing, tools, and interests coexisting
avoid: making the root feel like a blog index only

copy_rules: Show routes and objects before claims.
Leave enough unsaid that clicking feels natural.
Do not add generic categories like work, writing, systems, experiments unless the objects demand them.

experience_contract.first_screen: Name plus a small set of touchable objects or doors, not a full bio.
experience_contract.navigation_model: Spatial object index: grouped by proximity, icon, motion, and placement instead of visible category headings.
experience_contract.progressive_disclosure: Each tap should reveal the next layer on the right route; the root should not summarize every route.
interaction_requirements: The first three exits are obvious without headers.

layout: Mobile starts as a compact personal front room.
Desktop can loosen into an asymmetric table, shelf, or wall of selected objects.
Group boundaries may be cards, spacing, rails, or clusters, but not explanatory headings.
The root should feel curated, not exhaustive.
typography: Name can keep a distinctive display face if it feels personal.
Labels stay plain and highly readable.
No large marketing headline under the name.
Text scale must remain comfortable on phone.
color: Use warm neutrals only as a base, not the whole identity.
Allow small vivid accents on objects and motion states.
texture: Optional tactile surface, paper, or object texture if performance-safe.
No decorative orbs, blobs, or generic gradients.
Texture must support the personal front-room idea.
density: Less polished air than the current template.
At least one below-fold hint should be visible on common mobile viewports.

motion_contract.policy: Motion may create curiosity and prove craft, but the page must work without it.
allowed: optional future Anime.js-style prototype only after static layout works
forbidden: heavy dependency before a measured need exists

invariants: No private photos, private locations, or private feeds.
Social/media modules require explicit public-review status before activation.

implementation_scope.build_status: Do not build until this contract is reviewed and approved.
implementation_scope.activation_rule: Only activate after mobile and desktop screenshots beat link-index-mobile-first for curiosity without losing clarity.

selection_criteria: Makes the viewer want to click further within five seconds.
Feels less polished and more alive than the current root.
Still reads as organized and trustworthy.
Serves professional and personal audiences through route choice rather than separate landing pages.
Can become a reusable contract model for future personal or small-business sites.
